questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why people tell stories and what makes a story work
How to write a scary story that frightens your friends
The history of the Cinderella story in different countries
Why children don't read books any more at home
questions.why: They discuss storytelling as a powerful way to connect and why we've told stories for millennia.

questions.q: How does Georgina react to Neil's first story about the mirror?
options: She laughs at it because it's so silly
She says it's boring and far too long
She asks him to stop because it's scaring her
She says she has heard it many times before
questions.why: Georgina says, 'Agh, stop Neil! You're scaring me!'

questions.q: What does Georgina say stories help us do?
options: Learn new words
Fall asleep more easily
Remember historical dates
Make sense of the world
questions.why: She says stories help us make sense of the world.

questions.q: According to Sandra Newman and other academics, how many classic plotlines are there?
options: Three
Seven
Twelve
Over 200
questions.why: Neil says there are seven classic plotlines which are constantly being recycled.

questions.q: According to Professor Jamie Tarani, why do we pass on classic stories?
options: They connect with fantasies and fears shared by all humans
They are short and easy to remember, even for children
Parents are told to read them to their children by teachers
They show us the real world exactly as it is, without magic
questions.why: He says stories tap into universal human fantasies and fears that go beyond particular times and places.

questions.q: What does Professor Tarani say about endings in most stories?
options: They are usually sad
They are usually surprising
They are just like real life
Good people usually win
questions.why: He says most of the time the bad guys have unhappy endings and the good guys happy ones.

questions.q: According to Sandra Newman, what happens when a storyteller rambles and doesn't get to the point?
options: Listeners start to ask lots of difficult questions
Listeners lose interest and even become hostile
Listeners enjoy the story more because it's longer
Listeners fall asleep before the story ends
questions.why: She says you see everybody lose interest and become hostile and frustrated.

questions.q: Why does Georgina say 'Oh, do get to the point, Neil!' near the end?
options: She is really angry with Neil and wants him to leave
She has to leave early for an important meeting
She's joking, as Neil is slow like a bad storyteller
She didn't understand the question and needs help
questions.why: Neil pauses before the answer, and she uses the phrase just discussed about storytellers.
